Q: DLL load failed while importing QtWebEngineWidgets error in PyQt6 A:

This is probably due to the PyQt6 and PyQt6-WebEngine's version mismatch. For me this solved the problem:

pip install --upgrade PyQt6 PyQt6-WebEngine

This command forces PyQt6 and PyQt6-WebEngine to upgrade to the latest version.

Q: Simpel Tabl Unld in Native Python A:

High-Performance Oracle Table Unloader

"High" is a nice adjective. But it is not quantitative; you've not told us how many rows/second on some reference workload. Minimally, please offer a URL # comment that shows some benchmark results.

ROWID ... (no primary key needed)

My personal philosophy is that every table deserves a PK, or else we should just leave it as a .CSV text file. But here, it seems that ROWID is standing in as your PK, allowing you to uniquely identify which row should go to which worker. It's not clear that the mention of "no PK!" in your marketing material is an important part of why someone would choose to adopt this library. If they neglected to define a PK, perhaps they'd have trouble seeing why that marketing claim applies to them. It is seldom that we see an RDBMS requirements document which says up front that there shall be no PK on a giant table. If things are dicey the DBA will typically just synthesize some integer ID column.

I note in passing that WHERE true can be a convenient default. And then we might tack on WHERE true AND ...

                    if not rows:

Consider reducing that to

                while rows := cursor.fetchmany():

Q: Which multimodal model is best for generating product category and description from an image only? A:

(a) single VLM can do both the tasks like Qwen2.5-VL or LLaVa based on the prompt structure.

or (b) you can split the pipeline clip style model(CLIP/SigLIP) for category and Qwen2.5-VL for description.

Q: VBA Macro migration tool into Python A:

Full disclosure: I built VBAtoPython.com, so weigh that accordingly — but it's aimed squarely at your situation.

One workflow note: it doesn't ingest an .xlsm directly. Export the modules first (VBA editor → Alt+F11 → right-click each module → Export) to get .bas/.cls files, then upload or paste those.

It's free up to 100 lines per module; file upload and batch conversion — useful for 40 modules — are on the paid tier. The engine is deterministic (same VBA in, same Python out) and it flags constructs like GoTo, On Error and COM calls for manual review instead of guessing at them. That last part matters in your case, since some of these macros were written by teammates whose logic you can't fully vouch for.

I'd be happy to run a couple of your trickier modules through and share the output if it helps.

Q: Universal Links and AASA: How do you deal with caching during development? A:

Yes, if the path matches the AASA file and the associated domains configuration is correct, the app should generally open even without any explicit URL-handling code.

What you're running into is likely AASA caching. Since iOS 14, Apple has used a CDN as part of the Universal Links infrastructure, and changes to the AASA file can take time to propagate. As a result, adding or removing paths may not take effect immediately, and reinstalling the app, restarting the device, or clearing Safari data often does not force a refresh.

For development, one useful option is to enable Developer Mode for Associated Domains by appending ?mode=developer to the domain in your Associated Domains entitlement, for example:

applinks:yourdomain.com?mode=developer

When used with a development build on a device with Developer Mode enabled, this can help bypass normal caching behavior and make AASA changes visible much more quickly.

You can also inspect the version Apple is serving through its CDN and compare it with the file hosted on your server to determine whether you're seeing a propagation delay or a configuration issue.

Q: Rewrite subquery with calculation to CASE expression A:

You could use the following statement with CASE provided you want to return a null when SUM(DAm) is null or 0.

(SELECT CASE
              WHEN SUM(DAm) IS NOT NULL and SUM(DAm)  <> 0 THEN (((SUM(DAm) - (SUM(StcCst) * -1)) * 100) /SUM(DAm))
              ELSE NULL
          END AS 'DG'
   FROM [F0001].[dbo].[ProdTr]
   WHERE AcYrPr = '201601'
     AND ProdTr.TrTp = 1
     AND [F0001].[dbo].[ProdTr].CustNo = '12773') AS dg_period_1
